title: Forti Halo
titleFull: Forti Halo, a flexible partition system | Phào Design
description: A movable partition system for workspaces, letting each person set how much cover they want. Graduation project in Industrial Design.
summary: A movable partition system for workspaces, letting each person adjust how much cover they have around their own seat.
materials: Aluminium and stainless steel frame, bamboo, wood or plastic ribs, woven fabric, frosted PVC curtain
heroAlt: The Forti Halo partition system set up in an open office
cardAlt: Forti Halo partition system in an office
altImageAlt: Forti Halo used as a private workspace and a team meeting pod

chapters.heading: The problem
body: Most office partitions are fixed in one position. Changing a seat or rearranging a room means taking them apart and putting them back, so in practice nobody does it.
Everyone ends up with exactly the amount of cover somebody else decided for them.
points: Fixed in place and hard to move
Little function beyond blocking a line of sight

images.alt: Survey of partition products currently on the market

chapters.heading: What users said
body: In interviews the two complaints that came up most were not about how partitions look. Both were about not being able to decide for yourself.
points: A sense of confinement when the direction of cover cannot be adjusted
Discomfort when the part you want covered is not, the face for example, or the legs when wearing a short skirt

chapters.heading: Structure: manual version
body: The screen is built from thin ribs, each 4 mm thick, with woven fabric stretched between them. The ribs can be bamboo, wood or plastic depending on what is available to manufacture.
Turning a geared knob extends or retracts the screen, so you can cover the area you actually want without standing up.

images.alt: Rib frame construction and gear knob mechanism of Forti Halo

chapters.heading: Structure: integrated version
body: Each column stands 2 m high with four stainless steel beams running through it, carrying the tension of the curtain and taking impact.
Bracing bars fold at 90 degrees to lock the columns into a stable frame. Wheels let the whole system be pushed with little effort, and adjustable feet keep it level on uneven floors.

images.alt: Column internals: bracing bar, through-column beams, wheels and adjustable feet

chapters.heading: In use
body: One frame, different curtains, different jobs. With a frosted PVC curtain, Forti Halo becomes a private workspace or a team meeting pod in the middle of an open office.
At a stadium it becomes a ticketing kiosk that goes up quickly, with a set of symbols showing whether a counter is open, closed or members only.

body: The project was built at full scale and exhibited alongside its technical drawings, pattern options and identity symbols.
